steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Cream butter and both sugars together in a mixing bowl until light and fluffy. Beat in egg and orange zest.

Stir flour, baking soda, and salt together in a separate bowl. Gradually mix flour mixture into butter mixture. Stir in white chocolate chips and walnuts. Drop tablespoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes in the preheated oven.
Remove from the oven and cool briefly on the baking sheets before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: White Chocolate Orange Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These white chocolate chip-studded cookies are bursting with fresh orange flavor. They’re my new personal favorites!

review.reviewBody: I also left out the nuts cause I don't like them and these are wonderful. I do have a little hint...if you like your cookies soft and fluffy, I use 1/2 baking powder and 1/2 baking soda. They do not fall flat and they stay moist and chewy. They are great this way. I will always make my cookies with 1/2 soda and 1/2 powder. Try it!!!

My son came over and stuck his hand in the cookie jar, took one bite and said, GREAT cookie mom! Tastes like biscotti! I thought they had a biscotti taste an texture as well. I used a fully packed Tbsp. of orange zest along with 1 1/2 tsp. orange flavoring, omitted the walnuts and added about a cup of crasins with only a cup of white chocolate chips. I used only a scant 1/2 cup of white and a scant 1/2 cup of brown sugar and liked that these cookies were not overly sweet. I did also add about a 1/4 cup more flour to make the dough the consistency of chocolate chip cookies. And instead of 3/4 tsp. baking soda, I added 1/2 tsp. baking soda and 1/4 tsp. baking powder. The cookies didn't spread much so I flattened them out "slighlty". I made nice lage cookies and baked them for 15 minutes. They were not at all dry, but had a biscotti texture and taste to them. They were gone in a day and I am now making another batch. My son asked me to give the recipe to his wife, so I went out and bought her a citrus zester and attached the recipe. Great gift! Thanks for the recipe!

I combined a bunch of the suggestions and added my own twist and ended up with an orange-white chocolate pecan sandy. I used half powder/half soda; packed the flour; used butter crisco; added both orange and vanilla extract; added the juice from the orange I zested; used pecans; and cut the chips in half.

What I did differently: I refrigerated the dough for a while, rolled it into balls, rolled them in sugar, and flattened them before baking. Mine took about 10-11 minutes to bake. I melted the other cup of white chocolate chips, added orange zest, and vanilla and orange extract and drizzled it over the cookies.

I'm really happy with the results. I think packing the flour allowed me to add the extra orange juice and not have the dough get runny. The final result tastes like a very orange pecan sandy with white chocolate chips and the chocolate drizzle has a subtle orange and vanilla flavor to it as well.

As a quick note, after refrigerating and because of the flour my dough was slightly crumbly, but working it into balls in my hands solved that problem.

I normally don't like cookies that are not super moist and chewy, but these are wonderful.

These were AMAZING. I made a few changes. I had no butter, so I used 1/2 c Crisco shortening and 2 T extra virgin coconut oil to add some crispness. Added a couple of capfuls of butter flavoring. I used 1/2 t each baking soda and powder, and added 2 little packets of True Orange, about 1/2 t of organic orange extract, and the zest of 2 small oranges for the orange flavoring. Whipped the shortening/oil/egg/sugars for about ten minutes. Decreased the nuts to 1/2 cup and the white chocolate chips to 1 cup. I then added some more True Orange to a bit of sugar, wet the bottom of a glass, and pressed down on the cookies before baking, giving them a lovely orange-sugared topping. Baked for about 11 minutes. It made 42 cookies at about 120 calories apiece, for those who count calories. They were INSANELY good!!!!! I cannot tell you how amazing these cookies were!

The best! 
 I make it 2-3 times a year(big batches) when our swimming club host meets and these have always been are winner. Crowds favorite! I Followed the recipe exact, just omit the nuts, because all baked goodies have to be nuts free and drizzled with little icing made out of :powder sugar with few drops water and few drops fresh squeezed lemon juice and lemon zest .
FOR THE PEOPLE who say the dough is dry, I also had this issue before, but once I watched a video how to properly measure flour, and I realized I always add more than the recipe calls. Since I watched that video I have never had an issue with any recipe. Just google and find if you make the mistake I used to make and if you measure the flour properly.

I love white chocolate and orange. However, after reading some reviews, I increased the orange zest and included the juice from the orange. I used the zest of an entire large orange and almost all of the juice from the large orange and a dash of vanilla. I would recommend tasting your wet ingredients mixture to decide how much more to add to your liking.

I enjoyed the flavour. I have always loved the combination of orange and chocolate but I found that there was too much flour and the presentation was not pleasing (pale)so, I will make the following 
changes next time. I will omit the white sugar and increase brown sugar to 1 1/2 cups, use the zest of a whole orange plus the juice of half the orange. I will cut the flour to 2 cups, add a tespoon of ginger and use semi-sweet choc. chips (personal preference). I also will baked at 375 F for 7-9 minutes for slightly crispier outer 'crust' while maintaining a chewy interior.

My new favorite cookie! I read previous reviews and made the following modifications: reduced flour to 2 cups, used 1/2 tsp baking soda and 1/4 tsp baking powder, used the zest of one medium orange (about 2 tbsp instead of 1 tbsp) and squeezed the juice from the orange in the the wet mixture and mixed before adding dry ingredients. I also cooked the cookies for 14 minutes. They came out a bit crisp with a nice orange scent and flavor.

Oh, man are these good! I doubled everything EXCEPT the zest and white chocolate. I cut up a 12oz bar of Ghirardelli and that was all it needed. As other reviewers suggested, I used half baking soda and half baking powder because I like soft cookies and I also threw in the juice of the orange I zested. Because I am making these for a 'fancier' occasion I am going to drizzle them with white chocolate (if there are any left! Hubby has been citing 'quality control' issues and has eaten about 5 of them already. I've never seen him eat more than 2 at a time, so that in itself is a great testament to this recipe!)

These were so delicious! I made them for a cookie exchange at work and got rave reviews. I used the grated rind of two navel oranges and didn’t measure it. I also added a half teaspoon of orange extract. I omitted the nuts and only used 1.5 cups white chocolate chips since some reviews said 2 cups were too many. The orange flavor was perfect and the texture of the cookies was exactly that of a standard chocolate chip cookie. I don’t know why some reviews are saying this was like biscotti. The recipe is very much a standard chocolate chip cookie recipe with slightly different flavors. I will definitely make these again!

I added 1/2 teaspoon of baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon of baking soda and orange juice from the orange I zested. I also added 1 tsp of vanilla extract. It was good but didn't taste much of the orange. Maybe orange extract would be better. I didn't have walnuts so didn't add it. It was a good cookie. I'll make it again and add orange juice, walnuts and orange extract.

This is a solid cookie, but it needs more orange flavor. I really couldn't pick up on it at all. If I had orange extract, I would have added some and I do think that would make the difference. Even so, it's a nice cookie and as others have said, is a lot like biscotti. I, too, used 1/2 tsp baking soda and 1/4 tsp baking powder. I left out the nuts because I don't like them and used dried cranberries. 1 cup of cranberries and 1 cup of chips was plenty of each. Tastes best with coffee!
Cookies crumbled after 1 day in container. I Love the white chips, but this has Way too many! There isn't enough dough for this much . Taste great.
I substituted sliced almonds for the walnuts (clean out the pantry recipe) and the more delicate taste worked very well.
So good
the recipe is great, but add 1/2 tablespoon of orange extract. The zest just doesn't give enough orange

This recipe was Ok but I think has potential of becoming really good. I could not add the orange zest but noticed it a bit grainy and cakey. The suggestions of using butter and shortening are great and should make up for the grainy texture. Some came out flat which was fixed by chilling the batter. I also used a lot less sugar than the recipe calls for as the white chocolate is already very sweet. Will make it again but with the suggestions plus hopefully next time I have the orange and its juice to add!
5 stars!
Excellent! I made half with walnuts half without, made exactly as recipe was written, new favorite!!!
Great recipe - I made a slight variation, with lime instead of orange. I added a half line worth of juice as well as peel, but I think the whole lime would have been better. Perfect cookies!
